implementation_notes: Since Java 8 the Collections Framework carries the predicate form: Collection.removeIf(filter) 'removes all of the elements of this collection that satisfy the given predicate' and returns whether anything was removed; the default implementation walks the collection with its own iterator, while platform collections override it where they can do better (ArrayList's hot loops compact and shift in bulk instead of removing one element at a time, immutable and fixed-size collections throw UnsupportedOperationException up front). There is no algorithm-plus-erase pair to compose - the collection owns both halves - so the classic C++ structure has no counterpart here beyond the pre-8 iterator loop (it.remove()) that is still the right tool when removal is interleaved with other per-element work. Use streams (collection.stream().filter(...).toList()) when a new collection is wanted; removeIf is O(n) in place with no extra allocation.
pitfalls: Collections that cannot change size throw UnsupportedOperationException: Arrays.asList(...) is fixed-size, List.of/Map.of are immutable (Java 9+), and unmodifiable or sublist views of immutable parents inherit the restriction - removeIf looks generic but fails at runtime.

LinkedList.removeIf unlinks node by node (no shifting, O(n) with a per-node removal) and CopyOnWriteArrayList.removeIf copies the whole array before removing: the compaction cost model does not carry over to every Collection implementation.
A predicate that mutates the collection throws ConcurrentModificationException, which is exactly the failure removeIf exists to replace for the for-each-plus-remove loop.
removeIf returns boolean, unlike C#'s RemoveAll count or C++20's std::erase_if size_type: code ported between ecosystems silently loses the number of removed elements.
sources: docs.oracle.com, java.util.Collection (Java SE 21) - removeIf 'Removes all of the elements of this collection that satisfy the given predicate', a default method since 1.8 that traverses the collection with its own iterator and throws UnsupportedOperationException when removal is unsupported: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Collection.html
